title: 942. Tallest Billboard

examples.explanation: Splitting into [1,2,3] and [6] gives two supports of height 6, which is the best achievable balance.
Grouping [2,3,5] against [4,6] (or [1,4,5] against [2,3,... ]) reaches height 10; nothing taller balances.
No two disjoint non-empty groups share a total, so the answer is 0.

hints: Track the height difference between the two supports instead of both heights.
Let dp[d] be the tallest higher-support height reachable with difference d, and update it rod by rod.
Adding a rod to the shorter support only raises the taller height when the rod overtakes the gap.
